H1.note: one claim per gene the run lists for H1 (APOE, TREM2, PLCG2). Sign from the mechanism: variants that impair the APOE-TREM2-PLCG2 axis contribute to AD, so each gene lowers AD risk. The chain's first step is an unsigned 'binds' (polarity unknown), although the title says APOE 'activates' the signalling, so no arm can leave APOE.

H2.note: one claim per gene the run lists for H2 (MS4A4A, TREM2). Sign from the mechanism: loss-of-function MS4A4A variants relieve TREM2 inhibition and protect against AD; the title calls TREM2 signalling 'protective', and increased TREM2 activity offers protection

H3.note: one claim per gene the run lists for H3 (INPP5D, PLCG2). Sign from the mechanism: inhibiting INPP5D relieves PLCG2, and promoting PLCG2 signalling confers protection against AD

H4.note: sign from the mechanism: loss of ABI3 function worsens AD. The mechanism says 'worsening Alzheimer disease pathology' (severity), but the step says 'inhibits Alzheimer disease' like every other disease step of the run; aspect risk to match the step

findings.detail: All four hypotheses are 'confidence: high' while each is 'support: speculative' with empty supporting_evidence and contradicting_evidence; after curation only H1.1 (binding) and H2.1 keep any supporting citation, and no disease-end step keeps one.
The title says APOE 'activates' TREM2-PLCG2 signalling, but H1.1 is 'binds' with polarity unknown; the chain has no signed APOE link, so the H1 APOE claim has no route.

Nothing cited states TREM2 activates PLCG2: the STRING edge has experimental 0.00 (database and text-mining only), the UniProt TREM2 text never names PLCG2, and the CELLxGENE row is a detection fraction.

Nothing cited states INPP5D inhibits PLCG2: UniProt says only 'modulation of EGF-induced phospholipase C activity' (generic PLC, no direction), PMID:41633359 is about INPP5D suppressing RIPK1, and the STRING edge is unsigned; the mechanism's PIP3-to-PLCG2 recruitment link is uncited.

The gene-to-AD steps cite genome-wide hits on missense alleles (rs72824905-G OR 0.73 in PLCG2, rs75932628-T OR 2.22 in TREM2) but no cited text says whether those alleles raise or lower the gene's function, so the gene-level sign rests on uncited knowledge and the run's strongest data carries no weight on any arm.

PMID:42092345 is an Abi3 S212F knock-in giving a 'dysfunctional microglial state' and microglial loss; it neither says ABI3 is required for microglial activation nor that S212F is loss-of-function, and it reports an 'Abi3-high state that predisposes microglia to degeneration', which the run does not discuss.

PMID:28714976, cited for 'microglial activation inhibits AD', concludes that 'the microglia-mediated innate immune response contributes directly to the development of Alzheimer's disease'; read literally that is the positive direction (kept as refutes), though the authors may mean involvement, since the same study reports both risk and protective variants.

PMID:41633359, cited at H3.1, reports that 'microglial INPP5D deficiency promoted aging-dependent RIPK1-mediated development of neuronal TDP-43 pathology, neuronal loss, and motor dysfunction', in tension with H3's claim that inhibiting INPP5D protects against AD; the run lists no contradicting evidence.

Claim-level evidence: a cited text that bears on a hypothesis's overall claim (INPP5D loss worsens neurodegeneration, PMID:41633359) but on no single step has nowhere to go except a finding; it does not lower the H3 arm.

Five chain steps cite CELLxGENE detection fractions as evidence for binding, activation or inhibition; these show expression only. The run ignores the one striking contrast: PLCG2 is detected in 24.8% of AD-donor microglia vs 47.5% of normal-donor microglia.

All three GWAS rows are for the trait 'Alzheimer's disease, proxy Alzheimer's disease or related dementias' (GCST90704646), broader than AD; the exclusion categories have no slot for a proxy or by-family-history phenotype (parent_disease is the nearest).

PMID:41435829 states that 'MS4A4A limits microglia viability, phagocytosis, and lysosomal function' and that MS4A4A restrains TREM2 'by an indirect mechanism' via MS4A6A and DAP12; the chain compresses this to a direct MS4A4A-inhibits-TREM2 step and leaves the phagocytosis link, which the mechanism relies on, out of the chain.

Evidence taxon cannot say non-human primate, and one evidence item cannot hold mixed designs: PMID:41435829 perturbs MS4A4A in macrophages and microglia (in vitro), NHPs and a mouse amyloid model; recorded as mechanistic, taxon mouse.

H4's mechanism says loss of ABI3 'worsens Alzheimer disease pathology' (severity) while its step says microglial activation 'inhibits Alzheimer disease' and its evidence is risk GWAS; curated as risk to match the step.

Every step carries the same context cell type 'mature microglial cell' (CL:0002629); it limits nothing, so it was dropped rather than refining every node (a cell-type refinement of Alzheimer disease would be meaningless).
RNPS1 and LPIN2 are listed as unexplained; no hypothesis covers two of the eight query genes.

H1's title ends at 'microglial phagocytosis', and the cited UniProt TREM2 text says TREM2 is 'Required for microglial phagocytosis of apoptotic neurons', but the chain has no phagocytosis node: it jumps from PLCG2 straight to AD.

H4's title is about 'microglial plaque compaction', and the cited PMID:42092345 reports that Abi3 S212F 'reduced dense-core plaque compaction', but the chain has no plaque-compaction node: it goes ABI3 to microglial activation to AD, and the cited text supports neither of those steps.

H4's mechanism asserts loss of ABI3 function 'through the AD-associated S209F variant', but no cited text says S209F (rs616338-T, OR 1.31; PMID:28714976 calls it only 'a risk variant') is loss-of-function; PMID:42092345 says only that it 'regulates cytoskeletal dynamics' and produces a 'dysfunctional microglial state'.

audit.before: one claim: APOE →− AD risk; note 'TREM2 and PLCG2 are links in the chain, not separate claims'
audit.after: three claims: APOE, TREM2 and PLCG2, each →− AD risk
audit.reason: the guide asks for one claim per gene the hypothesis is about, and the run lists H1's genes as APOE, TREM2 and PLCG2. The mechanism gives each gene's direction: 'variants that impair this APOE-TREM2-PLCG2 axis ... contributing to Alzheimer disease pathogenesis'. With only the APOE claim, H1 tested nothing, because APOE has no signed step. The TREM2 and PLCG2 claims compose (S2→S3, S5, S3). The title_overstates_chain finding now names the APOE claim.

audit.after: two claims: MS4A4A →+ AD risk, TREM2 →− AD risk
audit.reason: the run lists H2's genes as MS4A4A and TREM2. The title calls TREM2 signalling 'protective', and the mechanism says that increasing TREM2 activity offers 'protection against Alzheimer disease'.

audit.after: two claims: INPP5D →+ AD risk, PLCG2 →− AD risk
audit.reason: the run lists H3's genes as INPP5D and PLCG2. The mechanism says that relieving INPP5D 'promotes PLCG2 signaling, and confers protection against Alzheimer disease'.

the record is not a bare expression level. It contrasts AD donors with normal donors (24.8% vs 47.5% of microglia), which is a signed expression difference. no_direction is for records that cannot carry a sign. This one can, and it is an association while the step claims an effect. It stays excluded.

audit.before: no finding that H1's chain drops its title's end node
audit.reason: the title ends at 'microglial phagocytosis', and the cited UniProt TREM2 text says TREM2 is 'Required for microglial phagocytosis of apoptotic neurons'. Yet the chain goes from PLCG2 directly to AD.

audit.before: no finding that H4's chain drops plaque compaction
audit.reason: the title is about plaque compaction, and the only literature cited for H4.1 (PMID:42092345) reports 'reduced dense-core plaque compaction'. The chain has no such node, and routes through microglial activation, which that text never mentions.

audit.before: variant_function_unstated covered H1.3, H2.2 and H3.2 only
audit.after: an added hypothesis-agent variant_function_unstated finding on H4.2
audit.reason: H4 is the one hypothesis whose mechanism asserts outright that a variant is loss-of-function ('Loss of ABI3 function, such as through the AD-associated S209F variant'). rs616338-T, PMID:28714976 and PMID:42092345 are all cited, and none of them says so.
